messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Application failed to start
parts:
Oh OK. The "RWebSocket unexpectedly closed" in this case is due to an incompatibility between fileInput and glimmer. We're looking into it. fileInput in general is quite flaky right now, if you hadn't noticed. (We're planning on rewriting it completely to be much more robust, but the websockets package we depend on needs to be overhauled first.)

As for the other app you have (that we discussed off-list) that crashes upon starting, the line "starting_value <- input$starting_value" appears outside of any reactive function, which is impossible. If you put input$starting_value directly where you're using it (in the reactive function) then that'd be fine.

If you do want to make a reusable expression based on input values, you need to make a reactive function.

On Thu, Dec 13, 2012 at 9:42 PM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
Oh OK. The "RWebSocket unexpectedly closed" in this case is due to an incompatibility between fileInput and glimmer. We're looking into it. fileInput in general is quite flaky right now, if you hadn't noticed. (We're planning on rewriting it completely to be much more robust, but the websockets package we depend on needs to be overhauled first.)

As for the other app you have (that we discussed off-list) that crashes upon starting, the line "starting_value <- input$starting_value" appears outside of any reactive function, which is impossible. If you put input$starting_value directly where you're using it (in the reactive function) then that'd be fine.

If you do want to make a reusable expression based on input values, you need to make a reactive function.
